outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected Tuesday into Tuesday night from portions of the southern Great Plains to the upper Mississippi Valley, with the greatest severe weather risk from southwest Kansas into western Oklahoma and the eastern Texas Panhandle. Very large and damaging hail and a few tornadoes are expected from late afternoon through evening. A strong tornado is possible. Damaging winds will be of particular concern from northern Kansas across eastern Nebraska and into western Iowa. Hail and wind are also expected overnight, across much of western and central Texas into Oklahoma.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A powerful upper trough will move across the Four Corners region during the day, with mid and upper level jets nosing into the southern Plains by late afternoon. To the east, an upper ridge will remain situated over the southeastern states, with fast southwesterly flow aloft rounding the ridge across the Upper Mississippi Valley. At the surface, a low pressure trough will extend from southern MN into the central High Plains by Tuesday afternoon, with primary surface low deepening across western Kansas and into Nebraska through the period. Substantial southerly low-level flow will persist across the Plains around the southeastern high, aiding in northward moisture return. Monday evening soundings indicate a moist boundary layer across south Texas, and this moisture will rapidly shift northward during the day on Tuesday. Strong destabilization will occur as a result of increasing moisture, surface heating, and cooling aloft, with a large area of severe thunderstorm potential from Texas into the Upper Mississippi Valley. ...Southwest Kansas southward into the eastern Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma... A deepening surface trough across the High Plains will sharpen the dryline, whi

sections.title: West/northwest Texas into central Oklahoma // Tuesday night
sections.text: As the upper trough continues to near, cooling aloft will eventually result in a rapid overturning of the unstable air mass across much of western Texas, from near the Rio Grande into Oklahoma. While supercells are possible initially, along with large hail, veering winds with the cold front should result in a largely linear storm mode with time. Both damaging winds and hail will be possible as activity moves to near I-35 by 12Z Wed. ..Jewell.. 05/16/2017

outlooks.summary: Episodes of severe thunderstorms are expected today and tonight within a swath from west Texas across the central Plains to the western Corn Belt and mid Missouri Valley. Tornadoes, severe gusts, and large, damaging hail are expected within this corridor.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Progressive synoptic-scale troughing will dominate the upper-air pattern today over the western/central U.S., with two primary/embedded perturbations influencing low-level mass fields and convective potential: 1. A strong, compact, mid/upper-level cyclone -- now apparent in moisture-channel imagery over Vancouver Island, forecast to move southeastward to southern ID by the end of the period. As heights fall across the northwestern U.S. and Great Basin ahead of that feature... 2. A strong shortwave trough, with embedded 500-mb low over southern NV at this time, will pivot eastward then east-northeastward across the Four Corners and northwestern MX. By 12Z, the trough should extend from eastern CO across eastern NM and far west TX. The 11Z surface analysis showed a surface low over northeastern SD, warm front from there across northeastern IA and southern Lake Michigan, and cold front southwestward across central NE to northeastern Co, and a reinforcing cold front over central SD and south-central WY. A wavy dryline was drawn from near IML southward across the KS/CO border area to the western TX Panhandle, southeastern NM and far west TX. The SD low should move northeastward across M

sections.title: Midafternoon into evening: Southern Plains dryline
sections.text: In mid/late afternoon, several discrete to semi-discrete supercells are expected to develop and move northeastward at 25-35 kt off the dryline. As this activity crosses the eastern Panhandle region, northwest TX, and parts of western OK, it will offer tornadoes, very large/damaging hail and sporadic severe gusts. Some giant (3-inch or more) hail is possible, along with potential for a couple of strong, relatively long-lasting tornadoes, from the mature phases of at least one or two cyclic supercells within convective arc. The all-hazards threat from these storms should last at least an hour or two into early evening, when the low-level jet increases and enlarges hodographs, and before the boundary layer stabilizes too much to permit sustained surface-based inflow. Thereafter, these supercells should spin down over western OK and northwest TX, south of the relatively fresh/cold outflow from the KS complex. Te environment will be characterized by strong surface heating and mixing along the dryline, with forecast soundings suggesting: near-zero MLCINH as early as around 20Z, 60s F surface dew points beneath steep midlevel lapse rates, 2500-3500 J/kg MLCAPE in a narrow plume ahead of t

sections.title: Overnight: Southern Plains front/dryline
sections.text: A mixture of initially discrete supercells and a band of thunderstorms should develop along the dryline and the overtaking front this evening and tonight. Any supercells will pose the risk of large, damaging hail, given the available moisture, large lapse rates/buoyancy, and favorable deep shear. Frontogenetic forcing and large-scale DCVA/cooling aloft will impinge on the moist sector and lead to a mostly quasi-linear belt of convection overnight, with damaging wind becoming the dominant threat before the activity encounters increasing CINH and weakening LLJ-related storm-relative flow late overnight. A tornado or two cannot be ruled out throughout either phase as well. ..Edwards/Dial.. 05/16/2017

outlooks.summary: Multiple clusters of severe thunderstorms are expected this afternoon and tonight within a swath from west Texas across the central Plains to the western Corn Belt and mid Missouri Valley. Tornadoes, severe gusts, and large, damaging hail are expected within this corridor. The greatest threat of a strong tornado or two appears to be focused over parts of western Oklahoma and the eastern Texas Panhandle.

sections.title: KS/NEB/IA/MO
sections.text: Morning water vapor loop shows a deep trough over the western states, with a leading shortwave impulse rotating across NM. 12z model solutions remain consistent that a cluster of intense thunderstorms will develop by mid afternoon over parts of southwest KS as this shortwave trough approaches. Strong heating is occurring in this region, with afternoon MLCAPE values over 3000 J/kg and minimal cap. Initial storms will likely be capable of very large hail and isolated tornadoes, but it seems likely that rapid upscale growth into a fast-moving squall line will occur. This will enhance the risk of damaging winds as storms spread northeastward across central/eastern KS and into parts of NE/IA/MO. If storm-scale trends dictate, this area may be considered for an upgrade to MDT risk in later updates.

sections.title: Western OK/TX Panhandle
sections.text: Low level moisture continues to stream rapidly northward into the TX Panhandle and western OK, with dewpoints now in the mid 60s across the region. Model forecast soundings by mid-late afternoon suggest strong instability will be present with MLCAPE values over 3500 J/kg and 8 C/km lapse rates. Isolated and discrete convection is expected to form along the dryline in the TX Panhandle and track northeastward through the mid-evening. A pocket of strong low-level shear is forecast to develop in this region, resulting in favorable hodograph structures for supercells capable of very large hail and strong tornadoes. Therefore have upgraded this area to MDT risk.

sections.title: West TX
sections.text: Later this evening, thunderstorms will likely develop southward along the dryline/cold front across parts of west TX. Large hail and damaging winds are expected with these storms. However, this activity is not expected to develop until well after dark when the capping inversion will be strengthening. This may tend to somewhat limit the coverage of severe storms. The line of storms will spread eastward and into west-central TX overnight.

sections.title: MN/WI/Upper MI
sections.text: A shortwave trough over the eastern Dakotas will track eastward and help to maintain scattered thunderstorms over parts of the western Great Lakes region. Breaks in the clouds will help to destabilize this area, and may lead to a few strong/severe storms later this afternoon and evening. Forecast soundings suggest sufficient vertical shear and CAPE to pose a risk of hail and damaging winds in the strongest cells. An isolated tornado is also possible. ..Hart/Dean.. 05/16/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms will impact much of the southern high Plains, northeastward through the middle Missouri Valley and portions of the Upper Midwest, late this afternoon into tonight. This includes the risk for a few tornadoes, particularly across parts of the eastern Texas and Oklahoma Panhandle region, damaging wind gusts and large hail.

sections.title: 20Z Outlook Update
sections.text: Adjustments to the 1630Z outlook have been mostly confined to the categorical/10 percent thunder line to account for latest model output and ongoing trends in destabilization. Highest severe probabilities appear to coincide the corridor of stronger surface heating near/east of the surface trough axis across the southern and central high Plains into the upper Mississippi Valley. This has become focused on the western/ northern periphery of a plume of warm and capping elevated mixed layer air now across much of the lower southern and central Plains into adjacent portions of the Mississippi Valley (and appears roughly delineated by the 10-12C 700 mb temps). Weakening inhibition associated with insolation and low-level moisture advection on the western edge of this environment is already allowing for increasing discrete storm development across the Texas/Oklahoma Panhandle region. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms will impact parts of the southern high Plains northeastward through the middle Missouri Valley and portions of the Upper Midwest this evening and overnight. This includes the risk for a few tornadoes across far western Oklahoma, southern Kansas, and northwest Texas. A localized tornado and wind threat will also persist over northern Wisconsin, with sporadic severe hail and wind possible from central Texas into Oklahoma overnight.

sections.title: Southern High Plains
sections.text: Several supercells, some possibly tornadic and with significant hail, persist across far western Oklahoma, and across parts of southwest Kansas. Capping becomes a concern with eastward extent, and as these cells move farther away from their warm air source region to the west. However, some redevelopment is not out of the question behind this activity as the low level jet increases and cooling aloft continues. Therefore, have maintained severe probabilities into the eastern Texas panhandle for this evening. To the south, isolated thunderstorm development was occurring over parts of west-central Texas along the dryline where a very warm air mass resides. Storms are currently supercells but convergence will continue to increase this evening as a cold front eventually surges eastward. Until then, significant hail and a couple tornadoes remain possible across northwest Texas which is also near the centroid of maximum instability. Then, a wind threat may progress across TX/OK.

sections.title: Minnesota into Wisconsin
sections.text: A cluster of severe storms associated with a disturbance rounding the ridge and near a weak surface low continues to develop eastward across northern Wisconsin. One particular supercell contains a tornado threat, and this threat may persist for 2-3 more hours as storms continue east across the state. Downstream of these cells, ample instability remains, with an impressive 40-50 kt low-level jet will be maintained as well, although veering with time. Tornadoes, damaging wind, and hail are all possible. As such, have upgraded a corridor to Enhanced Risk for isolated tornadoes and wind damage.

sections.title: Central Kansas across southeast Nebraska and into Iowa
sections.text: A large number of storms continue to evolve northeastward out of central Kansas and into southern and eastern Nebraska, with significant wind measured in the Omaha area. The area continues to be very unstable with the warmest temperatures currently in Iowa. This environment should continue to support damaging outflow winds with multiple clusters of cells through the evening. Hail is also likely with the strongest cells. ..Jewell.. 05/17/2017

mesoscale_discussions.summary: While considerable uncertainty remains, there is some potential for an uptick in storm intensity this afternoon, with a conditional risk of large hail and a tornado or two with the strongest cells.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A modest increase in ongoing elevated thunderstorm activity has recently been noted across far southeast MN into western WI. This activity is occurring in the vicinity of a convectively-induced vort max that will move east-northeast across central WI this afternoon. It remains unclear whether the ongoing storms will become rooted in the boundary layer and intensify, or if new surface-based convection will develop, though some heating and moistening across central WI will support the potential for surface-based activity to evolve with time. Moderate instability and a favorable wind profile (noted in KARX VWP data) will favor supercell development with any surface-based convection, with a resulting threat of large hail and a tornado or two, especially in the vicinity of an outflow boundary draped across central WI. Considerable uncertainty remains regarding the short-term threat, but watch issuance will be considered if the supercell threat appears to be increasing.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms will develop across the eastern TX/OK Panhandles over the next few hours. Tornadoes are expected with this activity, along with very large hail and severe wind gusts. Tornado watch will be issued by mid afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest visible satellite imagery suggests large-scale forcing for ascent is spreading across the southern Rockies, per marked increase in showers and thunderstorms over western/central NM. Downstream, dry line has mixed east and is becoming well defined over the TX Panhandle/South Plains region with substantial boundary-layer cu immediately east of the dry line. Towering cu, and a few attempts at glaciation, are noted over Hutchinson/Hansford/Ochiltree Counties. There is increasing confidence supercells will develop across the eastern TX/OK Panhandles by mid afternoon with subsequent movement expected into western portions of OK/southwest KS into the evening. Environmental conditions appear favorable for tornadoes and very large hail as steep lapse rates are evident on 12z soundings and surface dew points have now risen into the mid 60s. Environmental conditions appear favorable for a few strong tornadoes.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected to develop across much of western and central Kansas this afternoon. Large hail and isolated tornadoes are likely, along with some damaging winds. Tornado watch will be issued shortly.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Higher quality boundary-layer moisture is advecting north across the central Plains early this afternoon, per deepening/expanding cu field. Dry line should sharpen and retreat slightly over western Kansas over the next few hours and supercells are expected to develop beneath agitated mid-level convection currently expanding across this region. It's not entirely clear what is causing this mid-level convection but low-level moistening, and cooling aloft should minimize CINH such that convection should increase and expand northeast into the early evening hours. Very large hail and isolated tornadoes appear likely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few strong to potentially severe thunderstorms are possible this afternoon with a threat of large hail and strong wind gusts. The magnitude and coverage of the threat appears too low for watch issuance at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A few strong thunderstorms have recently developed to the east of Denver, with other convection attempting to develop to the northwest across the higher terrain. As large-scale ascent continues to increase ahead of a strong upper trough over the Southwest, an increase in thunderstorm coverage and intensity is expected later this afternoon. While low-level moisture is quite marginal, continued heating will result in marginal SBCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg, which will combine with vertically veering wind profiles to support the threat of a few organized structures and perhaps a supercell or two. A few instances of large hail and/or strong wind gusts will be possible with the strongest cells, though the overall coverage and magnitude of the threat is expected to remain too low for watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: One or bands of strong/potentially severe thunderstorms will be possible this afternoon into early evening. Watch issuance is currently being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong thunderstorm development has recently occurred south of the Twin Cities area, while some intensification has recently been noted with the band of storms approaching Green Bay. The eastern activity continues to be associated with a weak MCV, while the mechanism for the development near MSP is not immediately clear. The nebulous surface and upper-air pattern continues to result in uncertainty regarding the convective evolution across this area in the short term. With time, toward evening, additional thunderstorm development is possible along and ahead of a cold front as an upper trough begins to approach from the southwest. Moderate instability and sufficient effective shear will continue to support the potential for organized storm structures, with a threat of large hail and locally damaging wind with any sustained discrete supercells. A tornado or two will also be possible, especially near a remnant outflow boundary from far southeast MN into central WI where surface winds are locally backed. Watch issuance is currently being considered.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Tornado threat should increase across the eastern TX Panhandle over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Boundary-layer lapse rates are steepening along the immediate moist side of the dry line as considerable breaks in cloud cover are noted across the eastern TX Panhandle. As surface temperatures warm, buoyancy is increasing across moist upslope regions of the southern High Plains. Over the last half hour or so, convection has markedly increased from Briscoe County to Gray County. It appears discrete supercells should mature across this region over the next few hours and attendant tornado threat should increase, especially along/north of a boundary draped from Childress County to Armstrong County. ..Darrow.. 05/16/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: While some uncertainty remains regarding the timing and mode of thunderstorm initiation, severe thunderstorm development is expected by late afternoon. Watch issuance is expected within the next hour.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At 2045Z, a persistent area of elevated convection continues over north-central KS, with recent intensification noted across Jewell county, while some boundary-layer cumulus development has recently been noted across southeast NE into western IA. As the influence of an upper trough begins to spread over the area from the southwest, an increase in the intensity of the elevated convection is possible, with some potential for this activity becoming rooted in the boundary layer. In addition, thunderstorm development is expected later this afternoon along a cold front draped from northwest IA through northeast/central NE into northwest KS. Strong diurnal heating and steep low-level lapse rates are resulting in moderate-to-strong buoyancy across the region, with MLCAPE of 2000-3500 J/kg noted in recent mesoanalyses. Strong midlevel southwesterly flow is resulting in effective shear of 40-50 kts, which is more than sufficient for organized storm structures. The potential for focused initiation along the cold front, along with a cluster potentially evolving from elevated convection over northern KS, may result in one or more bowing structures capable of an enhanced damaging wind threat, in addition to potentially significant hail. The potential for sustained discrete supercells is more uncertain, but any such activity would pose a threat of a tornado or two, especially toward evening when boundary-layer moisture and low-level shear become more favorable. Despite the uncertainty regarding the exact timing and mode of the severe threat, the eventual magnitude and coverage of the threat will necessitate watch issuance, potentially within the hour.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for very large to giant hail (2-3.5 inches in diameter) and tornadoes will increase nonlinearly (22-00Z). A large/intense (EF3+ capable) tornado is possible (23-02Z) given the strengthening low-level shear, very large buoyancy, and the mature phase of a quasi-discrete supercell.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar imagery shows a north-south cluster of supercells over the eastern TX Panhandle which have moved east of the dryline. OK and West TX mesonet observations show dewpoints in the 66-69 degrees F range and temperatures in the middle 70s to around 80. Very strong backing of low-level flow, perhaps partially induced by parent storms to the west, has enlarged the low-level hodograph size during the past 30 minutes from Childress County to Wheeler County with 2-4 mb/hour falls in the past 2 hours. RAP forecast soundings show 0-1 km SRH increasing from 150 m2/s2 to 350 m2/s2 (locally higher and augmented by storms) during the 22-00Z period. As the low-level shear continues to increase over the next couple of hours, expect with medium to higher confidence of a large/intense tornado ---potentially capable of EF3+ intensity--- evolving from supercell cluster in Wheeler/Gray/Collingsworth counties.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A watch will probably be required within 1-2 hours. Very large hail and perhaps a tornado are possible. The potential for severe gusts will increase later this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows a couple of weak updrafts and the initial stages of convective initiation trying to occur along the dryline over the Permian Basin. Water vapor imagery suggests the leading edge of stronger ascent is beginning to move into the Permian Basin as a potent mid-level shortwave trough over the Desert Southwest pivots east into the southern High Plains tonight. Surface temperatures have warmed into the upper 80s and lower 90s degrees F east of the dryline and considerable mixing has occurred with dewpoints ranging from the lower 50s near I-20 to the upper 60s near the Rio Grande. Very strong effective shear 60-80 kt and 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE will support rapid storm organization into supercells once storms develop. As the low-level jet intensifies this evening and ascent strengthens further, a convective band is forecast to evolve. Hail and wind will become the primary risks once this transition occurs.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Convection will migrate into the region from the west and southwest over the next few hours. Some thunderstorm development is also underway near/northwest of North Platte. A severe thunderstorm watch is being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong to occasionally severe convection continues to migrate northeastward into western portions of the discussion area at this time. Newer updrafts are evident across west-central Nebraska via satellite and radar observations. These storms are in an upslope environment favorable for continued convective development, with steep mid-level lapse rates aloft atop 50s dewpoints favoring moderate instability (around 1000-1500 J/kg MUCAPE). Deep shear profiles favor some storm organization, although weak low-level shear will favor mostly outflow-dominate convection with primarily a severe wind and hail threat over at least the next two to three hours. If convective coverage of severe hail/wind increases, a severe thunderstorm watch may be needed.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A considerable tornado threat continues across the discussion area, including significant tornado potential with a cell currently over Rusk County, WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of intense thunderstorms with a history of strong rotation, significant hail, and tornadoes, has evolved over the past couple of hours in northwestern and north-central Wisconsin. Additional activity has matured west of this cluster from near DLH southward to about 25 SSE of MSP. These storms are moving into a favorable environment for continued significant severe potential (including tornadoes) over the next 1-2 hours, where recent objective analyses indicate 2000+ J/kg MUCAPE and 300-400 m2/s2 effective SRH downstream of this complex of storms within an undisturbed preconvective airmass. Based on the evolving severe threat, a new tornado watch and/or spatial extensions to the existing watch may be needed around/just after 00Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: It remains unclear how far east the tornado risk will develop with ongoing supercells in western OK. Large hail and some tornado risk will probably accompany the storms east of Tornado Watch 220 into parts of central OK.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows supercells over western OK with very large hail values per MRMS MESH with recent confirming reports. A likely strong tornado likely occurred around 0000-0015Z over west-central OK with the strongest velocity signature this evening. Stunted 0-2 km lapse rates (less than 6 degrees/km) and moderate low-level moisture (dewpoints ranging from 67 degrees F on the eastern edge of the Watch 220 to 65 degrees F on the I-35 corridor) will likely limit the tornado risk with further east extent towards the I-35 corridor compared to the ongoing potential over western OK. The 00Z OUN raob showed a stout capping inversion and large MLCINH (-300 J/kg). However, strong supercells and their internal dynamics may compensate to maintain some threat for a tornado immediately east of the current watch. With time, it appears the severe risk with the supercells as they move into central OK will transition to mainly hail/wind over central OK as storms move east of the moist axis. ..Smith.. 05/17/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across WW 224. A new WW downstream of 224 in portions of Iowa may be needed over the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered, primarily hail and wind producing thunderstorms continue across many areas in WW 224 at this time. Over the past hour, a bow echo has organized over eastern Nebraska that produced significant severe wind gusts near the Omaha area. That bow echo has organized further and accelerated into western Iowa into an airmass sufficiently unstable to sustain a severe wind and hail threat. Convective trends in this region suggest that a new, downstream severe thunderstorm watch may be needed in portions of Iowa after about 01Z. Farther southwest, multiple linear segments have evolved across southern Nebraska and north-central Kansas. These storms will continue to propagate north/northeastward in a pre-convective airmass characterized by moderate instability and 40-50 knots of deep shear, suggesting that a hail and severe wind threat will continue for several more hours. More isolated, cellular convection that can organize ahead of or separate from linear clusters may exhibit an isolated tornado threat, although most recent trends suggest that hail/wind will be the dominant severe threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Ongoing storms will pose a severe wind/hail and isolated tornado threat over the next 1-2 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Ongoing strong to severe thunderstorms continue across southern and eastern portions of WW 222 currently. These storms continue in an environment characterized by weak to moderate instability (500-1500 J/kg MUCAPE, strongest in western portions of the discussion area) and strong low-level shear (400 0-3 km storm relative helicity indicated on the ARX wind profiler) suggestive of a continued tornado threat across the region. Storms have evolved into clusters and localized linear segments that, when combined with 20F surface dewpoint depressions in most of the area and cooling surface temperatures, may act to mitigate the overall tornado threat somewhat. Nevertheless, at least an isolated tornado threat, in conjunction with a continued severe hail/wind threat, will continued through at least the scheduled expiration of WW 222 (0300Z). Beyond this point, some questions remain with the extent and character of the severe threat. The bulk of the threat may evolve into a hail threat with storms that persist in the region and storms become progressively more elevated with time atop a cooling nocturnal boundary layer. A mature linear complex over Iowa (responsible for significant wind gusts and hail earlier) will also approach southwestern portions of the watch in 2-3 hours. It is possible that a new severe thunderstorm watch will be needed after 03Z. This will be coordinated with affected local offices.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across portions of WWs 224 and 225. Considerable convective overturning has occurred in portions of Nebraska west of an ongoing convective complex in eastern parts of the state, and portions of WW 224 may be canceled early.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection has evolved into three expansive linear segments across portions of the discussion area - 1) across central Iowa, 2) extending from near Omaha, NE southeastward to near Salina, KS, and 3) in WW 225 from near Mullen, NE (MHN) southward to near Goodland, KS. Although nocturnal boundary layer cooling has commenced and led to a lessening of instability in much of the region, steep mid-level lapse rates aloft and organization of convection along propagating cold pools has sustained this activity, with a continued hail/wind threat in most areas. In portions of central/east-central Nebraska, significant convective overturning has occurred over the past several hours, with widespread stratiform precipitation occurring in that region. This overturning should diminish the overall severe threat in this region except for perhaps an isolated/marginally severe hail threat in northeastern Nebraska. As such, portions of WW 224 may be cancelled before the originally scheduled expiration time (05Z). Farther west, the threat across WW 225 should continue as storms propagate eastward, although it is currently uncertain how east these storms will maintain their current intensity given the low-level stabilization that has occurred downstream in portions of WW 224. The threat west of the convective line in WW 225 has diminished such that portions of that watch in western Nebraska may also be canceled early. Lastly, southward spatial extensions of WW 225 near/east of Goodland may be needed over the next hour or so as convection continues in that region.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A replacement watch (likely severe thunderstorm) will be issued very shortly.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A large hail/severe gust risk is forecast for this evening into the overnight.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered storms in the discussion area will continue to pose a wind gust/1" hail threat, although the overall threat should be on the wane over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several bands/linear segments of convection persist across WWs 227 and 228 despite lessening surface-based instability within the pre-convective environment supporting this activity. Weak to moderate instability exists - strongest in portions of Iowa - which may result in a continued threat for isolated wind damage along forward propagating segments in central Wisconsin, northeastern Iowa, and southern/central Iowa. Farther north into southeastern Minnesota and west-central Wisconsin, convection appears to be undercut by previous convection that moved through the region 1-2 hours ago. A lingering 1" hail threat will exist with stronger cores associated with this activity.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Watch 226 is scheduled to expire at 08Z. Watches 229-230 are scheduled to expire at 10Z. All may be cleared behind the primary swath of convection. Although isolated strong-severe gusts may extend just east of the watches, especially in OK and north TX, additional watches do not appear likely at this time. Some county-scale extensions of existing watches may be performed locally as convective trends warrant.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A swath of strong/isolated severe thunderstorms with several embedded bow/lewp formations and outflow-dominant quasi-linear structures is apparent from south-central KS across central OK, western parts of north-central TX, the Hill Country and Edwards Plateau. Although sufficient forced ascent from associated cold pools may sustain this convection east of the ongoing watch areas, the overall organized-severe threat is expected to dwindle through the remainder of the overnight hours. Objectively analyzed diagnostic fields suggest progressively stronger MLCINH and weaker MLCAPE currently exist with eastward extent, and that does not account for additional stabilization expected through further diabatic surface cooling. As such, the severe potential will continue to sort itself downscale into ever-smaller nodes along the leading edge of the activity, becoming more localized and marginal with time. Behind the line, cold advection and diabatic cooling together will render the air mass too stable for severe. ..Edwards.. 05/17/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
